findings.title: ground_wolf_companion_stat_block and ground_horse_companion_stat_block are ~150-line near-duplicates
findings.evidence: fn ground_wolf_companion_stat_block(id_prefix, owner_class_label, companion_level, explanations) at line 7200 and fn ground_horse_companion_stat_block(...) at line 7406 compute identical formulas (base_attack_bonus = hd*3/4, fort/reflex = hd/2+2, will = hd/3, strength_bonus/natural_armor via the shared animal_companion_* helpers, armor_class = 10+natural_armor, attack damage = 1.5x str mod floored, hp via animal_companion_hit_points) and push the same six explanation-record shapes with only species constants (WOLF_* vs HORSE_*) and one label swap (bite vs hoof) differing. ground_wolf_companion_link_and_share_spells_vacuous (7347) and ground_horse_companion_link_vacuous (7568) are the same pattern one level down. The module's own doc comment for companion_base_stat_table (line ~207) states this exact pair was already identified as the case a table-driven generalization should replace, but both hand-written copies are still present and still called from the compute-chassis dispatch (grep hits at lines ~36749/42779-equivalent outside this chunk use the same per-species pattern).
findings.fix_description: Route both through the already-existing companion_base_stat_table module (or a single ground_companion_stat_block(id_prefix, owner_class_label, companion_level, species: &CompanionSpecies, explanations) parameterized on species constants + primary-attack label) so the six-record shape is written once.
findings.risk_notes: The in-file doc comments (7380-7405) explicitly record that a prior review deliberately kept these separate to avoid any risk to Druid's/Hunter's already-shipped Wolf output when Cavalier Mount was added. Any consolidation must be proven byte-identical against the existing wolf/horse test fixtures before landing; this is exactly the kind of change the repo's own precedent (task #49 folding four Monk slow-fall consts into one formula) shows the team does eventually do once confidence is high, but it is not a mechanical/auto_fix-safe change.

findings.title: ground_ranger_combat_style_feat_pool and ground_sorcerer_bloodline_feat_pool share an identical 'grounded feat-pool' skeleton
findings.evidence: Both functions (fn ground_ranger_combat_style_feat_pool(level: u8, explanations: &mut Vec<ComputationExplanation>, diagnostics: &mut Vec<ComputationDiagnostic>) at 1520, and fn ground_sorcerer_bloodline_feat_pool(sorcerer_level: u8, explanations, diagnostics) at 2234) follow the identical shape: compute a slot_count from a level formula, push one ComputationExplanation with a slot_count==0 vs >0 templated detail string, early-return if 0, then loop over a static eligible-feat slice pushing one non-claim-blocking ComputationDiagnostic per feat with a templated 'not_modelled' message (with the sorcerer variant additionally skipping an exclusion list). The doc comments on both explicitly call out the shared 'ratified Fighter/Cavalier/Brawler/Arcane-bloodline treatment' precedent, implying more call sites of this same shape exist elsewhere in the file outside this chunk.
findings.fix_description: Extract a generic fn ground_feat_pool(id_prefix: &str, slot_count: i16, eligible: &[&str], exclusions: &[&str], detail_zero: impl FnOnce()->String, detail_nonzero: impl FnOnce()->String, explanations, diagnostics) and have both (and any Fighter/Cavalier/Brawler equivalents in other chunks) call it.
findings.risk_notes: Cross-chunk: search for other 'ground_.*_feat_pool' or hand-inlined equivalents (Fighter/Cavalier/Brawler bonus-feat pools) in chunks covering lines beyond 7592 before proposing a shared helper, since only 2 of the 4+ classes named in the doc comments have a same-named function inside this chunk.

findings.title: Repeated per-tier (LEVEL, CHOICE_ID[, SELECTION]) const triples for Paladin Mercy, Ranger Favored Enemy, and Ranger Favored Terrain would collapse into small static tables
findings.evidence: Paladin Mercy: PALADIN_MERCY_LEVEL/_CHOICE_ID (609,655) then PALADIN_{SECOND,THIRD,FOURTH,FIFTH,SIXTH}_MERCY_GRANT_LEVEL/_CHOICE_ID (668-707), 6 near-identical pairs. Ranger Favored Enemy: RANGER_FAVORED_ENEMY_{SECOND,THIRD,FOURTH,FIFTH}_INTERVAL_LEVEL/_CHOICE_ID plus matching BONUS_INCREASE_*_SELECTION consts (1038-1137), a 4-tier repeat. Ranger Favored Terrain: the identical shape again for terrain (1185-1279), a 4-tier repeat. Each tier's const pair differs only in its ordinal name and literal level/id string; the values are already effectively a table (interval = base + 5*n) that is hand-unrolled into ~30 named consts total across the three features.
findings.fix_description: Replace each family with a single &[(u8, &str)] (or a small struct slice) plus one small loop/lookup function, mirroring the pattern already used for HUNTER_ANIMAL_FOCUS_TIERED_OPTIONS (line 2631) and RANGER_COMBAT_STYLE_FEAT_POOL, and the precedent set by task #49's own consolidation of four Monk slow-fall consts into one formula (cited in this same file around line 6057).
findings.risk_notes: Every one of these consts is very likely referenced by name at its own call site and by name in test assertions and diagnostic-id strings elsewhere in the file (outside this chunk); a table swap must preserve every existing choice-id string and diagnostic id verbatim or it will regress corpus-facing diagnostics. Not auto-fixable.

findings.title: wolf_companion_hit_dice and horse_companion_hit_dice are byte-identical one-line wrappers
findings.evidence: fn wolf_companion_hit_dice(companion_level: u8) -> u8 { ANIMAL_COMPANION_HIT_DICE_BY_MASTER_LEVEL[animal_companion_table_index(companion_level)] } (7183-7185) and fn horse_companion_hit_dice(companion_level: u8) -> u8 { ANIMAL_COMPANION_HIT_DICE_BY_MASTER_LEVEL[animal_companion_table_index(companion_level)] } (7394-7396) have identical bodies; the doc comment on the horse variant (7380-7393) explains this is deliberate (kept separate so future edits to one never touch the other's call sites), so it is a named, intentional duplication rather than an oversight.
findings.fix_description: Could be folded into a single fn companion_hit_dice(companion_level: u8) -> u8 shared by both call sites if the team revisits the isolation tradeoff; not urgent given the explicit rationale already on record.
findings.risk_notes: Same isolation rationale as PC1-1; bundle with that fix rather than doing it alone.
